themebook.description: The themebook the card was built from, by name. Optional, because a card can outlive the book it came from and still be played.

theme_type.description: Which family the card belongs to. Required and without a default: it decides the banner, the motivation's grammar and the erosion track.

title.description: The title the player wrote at the top of the card.

motivation.description: The card's motivation, filled in. Absent on an Extra or a Crew card.

kind.description: Whether the card's motivation reads as a Mystery, an Identity, or neither.

text.description: The motivation the player wrote, the answer rather than the themebook's prompt. Supports inline Markdown.
examples: Who keeps answering when I ask?
I am the one who stays.

attention.description: The attention track, which fills as the theme is played and buys improvements.

filled.description: How many boxes are ticked right now.

maximum.description: How many boxes the track prints. Three on every card the books show, but an improvement can widen it.

erosion.description: The erosion track, Fade or Crack. Absent on an Extra or a Crew card, which do not erode.

kind.description: Fade on a Mythos card, Crack on a Logos one.

filled.description: How much the theme has eroded so far.

maximum.description: How much erosion the theme survives before it breaks.

power_tags.description: The power tags written on the card, in printed order.

text.description: The tag as the player wrote it on the card.

letter.description: Which themebook question this tag answers. Optional, because a homebrew tag has no question behind it.

question.description: Compatibility spelling used by Handbook for the same themebook question reference as `letter`.

is_burnt.description: Whether the tag has been burnt and is spent until it is recovered.

burnt.description: Compatibility spelling used by Handbook for the same burn mark as `is_burnt`.

items.description: One power tag on the card. The books' rule that an extra power tag costs an extra weakness tag is a play rule, not a constraint enforced here: a card mid-play can sit between the two.

weakness_tags.description: The weakness tags written on the card, in printed order.

text.description: The weakness as the player wrote it on the card.

letter.description: Which themebook question this weakness answers. Optional, for the same reason as a power tag's.

question.description: Compatibility spelling used by Handbook for the same themebook question reference as `letter`.

is_invoked.description: Whether the weakness has been invoked this session for its build-up.

items.description: One weakness tag on the card. Counted against the power tags by the books' rule, which the schema records rather than enforces.

improvements.description: The improvements available to this theme, ticked as they are bought. Unlike the themebook, a card lists only what it needs to: a partial list is normal.

name.description: The improvement's title, as the themebook names it.

effect.description: What the improvement does, copied onto the card so it can be read without the themebook. Supports inline Markdown.
examples: Take an additional power tag for this theme.

is_taken.description: Whether the player has bought it.

items.description: One improvement listed on the card, ticked once bought.

meta.description: Attribution and cataloging fields for the card's origin.

publication_type.description: Classifies the card's source to aid cataloging and tooling.

source.description: Source title where this card appears, if any.

authors.description: List of credited authors or contributors.

page.description: Page number (if relevant to the source).

description: City of Mist - a played theme card: a themebook's questions answered, with the tracks and the tags as they stand at the table. The blank questionnaire is the separate `theme-kit` target; this one exists on its own, because a card can be read without the themebook that produced it.
